1.word_for_word: एक-चत्वारिंशकेऽहन् रजकं प्राविशन् पुरीम् । — On the forty-first day Rajaka entered the city.; ततो वरान् अदात् तुष्टः सुदाम्नो वायकस्य च ॥ — Then, being pleased, Sudamna gave boons to Vāyaka.; स-शङ्कम् अक्रूर-मनः प्रबोध्य — awakening the mind of Akrura with that suspicion; स्व-धाम सन्दर्शन-सत्-कृपातः । — By the true grace of seeing one’s own abode.; स्व-राज-धानीं मथुराम् अपश्यद् — He saw Mathura, the capital of his kingdom; अलङ्कृटानन्त-महोत्सवाढ्याम् ॥१॥ — rich in ornaments and infinite festivals.
1.translation: On the forty-first day Rajaka entered the city. Then, being pleased, Sudamna gave boons to Vāyaka. awakening the mind of Akrura with that suspicion By the true grace of seeing one’s own abode. He saw Mathura, the capital of his kingdom rich in ornaments and infinite festivals.

4.word_for_word: भूमौ वियति जले वा यावन्त्य् अद्भुतानि तानि त्वय्य् एव सन्ति तं च त्वां पश्यतो मे किम् अद्भुतम् अदृष्टम् । — All the wonderful things on earth, in the sky or in the water are in You, and what wonderful thing have I not seen when I see You?; अपि तु सर्वं दृष्टम् इत्य् अर्थः ॥४॥ — Rather, it means that everything has been seen.
4.translation: All the wonderful things on earth, in the sky or in the water are in You, and what wonderful thing have I not seen when I see You? Rather, it means that everything has been seen.

5.word_for_word: ननु मत्-प्राप्तेः पूर्वम् एव त्वं विस्मित-मुखो लक्षितोऽसि, अतो भूमौ वियति जले व किम् अप्य् अद्भुतं दृष्टम् एवेति चेद् अत आह---यत्राद्भुतानीति । — If, indeed, you were noticed with a wonderful face before you came to Me, and therefore you have seen something wonderful on earth, in the sky, or in the water, then he says, "Where are wonders?"; यत्र त्वयि सर्वाण्य् अद्भुतानि सन्ति तं त्वाम् इह पश्यतो मेऽन्यत्र भूम्य्-आदौ किम् अद्भुतं दृष्टं, त्वां विना न तत्र किञ्चिद् अद्भुतम् इत्य् अर्थः । — What wonderful thing have I seen elsewhere in the beginning of the earth when I see You here, where all the wonderful things are in You, and without You there is nothing wonderful there?; ब्रह्मन् हे परमेश्वरेत्य् अर्थः । — Brahman, O God, means.; ब्रह्मेति वा पाठः ॥५॥ — or the text, Brahma.
5.translation: If, indeed, you were noticed with a wonderful face before you came to Me, and therefore you have seen something wonderful on earth, in the sky, or in the water, then he says, "Where are wonders?" What wonderful thing have I seen elsewhere in the beginning of the earth when I see You here, where all the wonderful things are in You, and without You there is nothing wonderful there? Brahman, O God, means. or the text, Brahma.

6.word_for_word: गान्दिनी-सुतोऽक्रूरः ॥६॥ — The son of Gandini was Akrura.
6.translation: The son of Gandini was Akrura.

7.word_for_word: दृष्टिं नाददुः । — They didn’t sound their eyes.; पश्यन्त एव स्थिता इत्य् अर्थः ॥७॥ — This means that they are still standing while they are watching.
7.translation: They didn’t sound their eyes. This means that they are still standing while they are watching.

8.word_for_word: राम-कृष्णागमनं प्रतीक्षमाणाः स्थिताः ॥८॥ — They stood there awaiting the arrival of Rama and Krishna
8.translation: They stood there awaiting the arrival of Rama and Krishna

10.word_for_word: स्व-गृहं च प्रविशताम् । — And let them enter their own houses.; अवमुच्योत्तार्य विश्राम्येत्य् अर्थः ॥१०.११॥ — This means that he should be released, lifted up and rested.
10.translation: And let them enter their own houses. This means that he should be released, lifted up and rested.

12.word_for_word: साग्रजः सह गोपालैर् इत्य् अर्थः ॥१२॥ — This means that he was with his elder brother and the cowherd men.
12.translation: This means that he was with his elder brother and the cowherd men.

13.word_for_word: यच्-छौचेन यस्य पाद-रजसः क्षालनोदकेन गृहाङ्गानस्थितेन ॥१३॥ — By washing the dust of the feet of the Lord with water which is situated in the courtyard of the house
13.translation: By washing the dust of the feet of the Lord with water which is situated in the courtyard of the house

14.word_for_word: श्लोक्यः पुण्य-कीर्त्य्-अर्हः । — The verse deserves a meritorious fame.; एकान्त-भक्तानां या गतिस् तां च लेभे ॥१४॥ — He also attained the destination of the solitary devotees.
14.translation: The verse deserves a meritorious fame. He also attained the destination of the solitary devotees.

15.word_for_word: अपुनन् पवित्रितवत्यः । — They have purified the Apunan.; याभिर् अद्भिः स्वः स्वर्गं प्राप्ताः ॥१५॥ — By which waters they have attained heaven.
15.translation: They have purified the Apunan. By which waters they have attained heaven.

16.word_for_word: प्रार्थयमानो नमस्करोति---देव-देवेति । — When praying, he bows down and says, “God, God.”; अतः परम् अन्य-च्छ्रेयो नास्तीति मत्वा बहुधा सम्बोधयति ॥१६॥ — He addresses them in many ways, thinking that there is no other good beyond this.
16.translation: When praying, he bows down and says, “God, God.” He addresses them in many ways, thinking that there is no other good beyond this.

17.word_for_word: आदौ तावद् यद् उचक्राय द्रुह्यतीति यदु-चक्र-ध्रुक् तं कंसं हत्वा सुहृदां प्रियं वितरिष्ये दास्यामि ॥१७॥ — In the beginning I shall kill Kaṁsa who is the enemy of the Yadu wheel and distribute whatever is pleasing to his friends
17.translation: In the beginning I shall kill Kaṁsa who is the enemy of the Yadu wheel and distribute whatever is pleasing to his friends

18.word_for_word: राम-कृष्णावानीताव् इति स्व-कृतं कर्मावेद्य समर्प्येति ॥१८॥ — Rama and Krishna have been brought, and he offers them his own deeds.
18.translation: Rama and Krishna have been brought, and he offers them his own deeds.

19.word_for_word: गोपैः परिवारितः प्राविशत् ॥१९॥ — Surrounded by the cowherd men he entered the city
19.translation: Surrounded by the cowherd men he entered the city

20.word_for_word: श्री-कृष्ण-दृष्टां पुरीम् अनुवर्णयति चतुर्भिः, ददर्श ताम् इति । — He describes the city that Sri Krishna saw in four ways, saying that he saw it.; स्फाटिकानि तुङ्गानि गोपुराणि पुर-द्वाराणि गृह-द्वाराणि च यस्यां ताम् । — She had crystal towers, city gates and house doors.; बृहन्ति हेममयानि कपाटानि तोरणानि च यस्यां ताम् । — The city had large golden doors and arches.; ताम्रं च आरः आर-कूटश् च तन् मयाः कोष्ठा धान्यागाराश्वशालादयो यस्यां ताम् । — The copper and the R and the R-coat are the cells in which the granaries, the horse stables and so on are made.; परिखाः परितः स्वात-गर्तास् ताभिर् दुरासदां दुर्गमाम् । — There were moats all around and swamp pits, and they made it difficult to reach.; उद्यानानि दूर-स्थानि वनानि रम्याण्य् उपवनानि च निकटानि तैर् उपशोभिताम् ॥२०॥ — They adorned the gardens far away with beautiful forests and suburbs nearby
20.translation: He describes the city that Sri Krishna saw in four ways, saying that he saw it. She had crystal towers, city gates and house doors. The city had large golden doors and arches. The copper and the R and the R-coat are the cells in which the granaries, the horse stables and so on are made. There were moats all around and swamp pits, and they made it difficult to reach. They adorned the gardens far away with beautiful forests and suburbs nearby

21.word_for_word: सौवर्णाः शृङ्गाटकाश् चतुष्-पथा हर्म्याणि धनिनां गृहाणि च निष्कुटा गृहोचिता आरामाश् च तैः । — They built palaces with golden gates on four streets and the houses of the rich were quiet and comfortable; श्रेणीनाम् एक-शिल्पोपजीविनां सभाभिरुपवेश-स्थानैर् अन्यैश् च भवनैर् गृहैर् उपस्कृताम् अलङ्कृताम् । — It was decorated with rows of single-craftsmen’s assemblies, seating areas and other buildings.; अमलाः स्फटिकाः । — Immaculate crystals.; हरितो मरकताः । — Green to emeralds.; वैदूर्यादि-रत्नैजुष्टेषु वलभ्यादिष्व् आविष्टैर् उपविष्टैः पारावतैर् बर्हिभिश् च नादिताम् । — The peacocks and peacocks resounded as they sat on their valves and other trees adorned with emerald and other precious stones.; तत्र वलभ्यो गृह-पुरो-भागेषु वक्र-दारु-च्छादनानि । — There are curved wooden roofs available in the front parts of the houses.; वेदयो वलभीनाम् अधो-देशे विरचिता अवष्टं भवेदिकाः । — The altars are arranged in the lower part of the valves and are placed on the altars.; जालामुख-रन्ध्राणि गवाक्ष-च्छिद्राणि । — There are holes in the mouth of the lattice and holes in the windows.; कुट्टिमानि मणि-बद्धा भूमयस् तेष्व् इति । — They are cut and the ground is bound with gems.; रथ्या राज-मार्गाः, आपणाः पण्यवीथयः, मार्गा अन्ये च, चत्वराण्य् अङ्गनानि, संसिक्तानि रथ्यादीनि यस्यां ताम् । — The streets are the royal roads, the shops are the marketplaces, the paths and others, the squares are the courtyards, the soaked streets and so on.; प्रकीर्णा माल्यादयो यस्यां ताम् । — She whose garlands and other things are scattered.
21.translation: They built palaces with golden gates on four streets and the houses of the rich were quiet and comfortable It was decorated with rows of single-craftsmen’s assemblies, seating areas and other buildings. Immaculate crystals. Green to emeralds. The peacocks and peacocks resounded as they sat on their valves and other trees adorned with emerald and other precious stones. There are curved wooden roofs available in the front parts of the houses. The altars are arranged in the lower part of the valves and are placed on the altars. There are holes in the mouth of the lattice and holes in the windows. They are cut and the ground is bound with gems. The streets are the royal roads, the shops are the marketplaces, the paths and others, the squares are the courtyards, the soaked streets and so on. She whose garlands and other things are scattered.

23.word_for_word: तथा स्वलङ्कृतानि द्वाराणि येषां ते गृहा यस्यां ताम् । — Similarly, the houses of those whose doors are well decorated; कैः । — Kaih.; आपूर्णैः कुम्भैर् दध्ना चन्दनेन चोक्षितैः सिक्तैः प्रसूनानां दीपानां चावलयो येषु तैः । — They placed pots full of flowers and lamps sprinkled with yogurt and sandalwood paste; वृन्दैः फल-गुच्छैर् उपलक्षिता रम्भाः क्रमुकाश् च तत् सहितैः । — The rambhas and kramukas were marked by clusters of fruit trees along with them; सकेतुभिः केतवो ध्वजास् तत् सहितैः । — The stars with their flags are accompanied by their stars; पट्टिका वितस्तिविस्तार-पट्ट-वस्त्राणि तत् सहितैः । — The strip was spread out and the fabrics were covered with wide stripes.; तत्रेयं रीतिः, द्वरेषूभयतस् तण्डुलानाम् उपरि कुम्भास् तत् परितः प्रसूनावलयः कण्ठे पट्टिका मुखे चूतादि-पल्लवास् तद् उपरि पात्रान्तरे दीपा-वलयस् तत् सन्निधौ रम्भाः क्रमुकाः केतवस् तोरणानि चेति । — There is this custom: on both sides of the doors are pots on top of the rice, a ring of flowers around it, a plaque around the neck, mango leaves in the mouth, a ring of lamps in another vessel above it.
23.translation: Similarly, the houses of those whose doors are well decorated Kaih. They placed pots full of flowers and lamps sprinkled with yogurt and sandalwood paste The rambhas and kramukas were marked by clusters of fruit trees along with them The stars with their flags are accompanied by their stars The strip was spread out and the fabrics were covered with wide stripes. There is this custom: on both sides of the doors are pots on top of the rice, a ring of flowers around it, a plaque around the neck, mango leaves in the mouth, a ring of lamps in another vessel above it.

24.word_for_word: नर-देव-वर्त्मना राज-मार्गेण तां पुरीं संप्रविष्टाव् इति द्वितीयान्तम् ॥२४॥ — The second end is that they entered that city by the royal path followed by men and gods.
24.translation: The second end is that they entered that city by the royal path followed by men and gods.

25.word_for_word: औत्सुक्यम् एवाह द्वयेन, काश्चिद् इति । — He said out of curiosity by two, some.; विपर्यक् विपरीतं धृतानि वस्त्राणि भूषणानि च यभिस् ताः । — They were wearing clothes and ornaments that were opposite to each other.; युगलेषु युग्म-धार्येषु कुण्डल-कङ्कणादिष्व् एकं विस्मृत्य समीयुः । — They came together in pairs, forgetting one of the earrings and bracelets they wore in pairs.; कृतम् एकम् एव पत्रं ययोस् ते श्रवणे यासाम्, एकम् एव नूपुरं चरणाभरणं यासां ताश् च ताश् च । — They wore the same leaf in their ears, the same anklets as their foot ornaments.; नाङ्क्त्वा अनङ्क्त्वा । — Not counting and not counting.; एकस्मिन्न् एव लोचने अञ्जनं निधायैव ॥२५॥ — Placing the ointment on the same eye.
25.translation: He said out of curiosity by two, some. They were wearing clothes and ornaments that were opposite to each other. They came together in pairs, forgetting one of the earrings and bracelets they wore in pairs. They wore the same leaf in their ears, the same anklets as their foot ornaments. Not counting and not counting. Placing the ointment on the same eye.

26.word_for_word: तद् भोजनं त्यक्त्वा अभ्यज्यमानाः सखीभिः क्रियमाण-तैलाभ्यङ्गाः अकृतोपमज्जना अकृतं स्नानाः । — They gave up that meal, rubbed themselves with the oil that their friends were doing, didn’t take a bath, didn’t take a bath.; अर्भं बालकम् । — The infant is a child.; अपोह्य निरस्य ॥२६॥ — removing and rejecting.
26.translation: They gave up that meal, rubbed themselves with the oil that their friends were doing, didn’t take a bath, didn’t take a bath. The infant is a child. removing and rejecting.

27.word_for_word: प्रगल्भा या लीलाः, ताभिर् हसितानि निरीक्षणानि च, तैः श्रियं रमयतीति श्री-रमणः, तेन आत्मना वपुषा तासां दृशाम् उत्सवं ददन् मनांसि जहार ॥२७॥ — The delight of the goddess of fortune, whose boastful pastimes, laughter and glances delighted the goddess of fortune, captured the minds of those women by celebrating their sights with his own body.
27.translation: The delight of the goddess of fortune, whose boastful pastimes, laughter and glances delighted the goddess of fortune, captured the minds of those women by celebrating their sights with his own body.

28.word_for_word: मुहुः श्रुतत्वात् तद्-गत-चेतसः सद्यस् तं दृष्ट्वा, तस्य प्रेक्षणं चोत्स्मितं च, तद् एव सुधा । — Having heard it again and again, his mind was immediately absorbed in it, and he looked at him and smiled, and that was the sweetness.; सुधा तयोक्षणं सेचनं, तेन लब्धो मानो याभिस् ताः । — The nectar is the irrigation of their eyes, and the honor they have gained by it.; दृशोद्घाटितेन नेत्र-द्वारेणात्मनि मनसि लब्धं प्राप्तं परिष्वज्य, तद्-अप्राप्ति-जनितम् अनन्तम् आधिं मानसीं व्यथां जहुः । — Through the eyes opened to sight, they embraced what they had found in their minds and gave up the infinite suffering and mental pain caused by not attaining it.; हे अरिन्दम ! — O Arindam!; निर्जित-कामेति सम्बोधनं शृङ्गार-रसे निमग्नो मा भूर् इति ॥२८॥ — The address, "You have conquered your desires," is, "Do not be immersed in the taste of aesthetics.
28.translation: Having heard it again and again, his mind was immediately absorbed in it, and he looked at him and smiled, and that was the sweetness. The nectar is the irrigation of their eyes, and the honor they have gained by it. Through the eyes opened to sight, they embraced what they had found in their minds and gave up the infinite suffering and mental pain caused by not attaining it. O Arindam! The address, "You have conquered your desires," is, "Do not be immersed in the taste of aesthetics.

29.word_for_word: सौमनस्यैः कुसुम-समूहैः शोभन-मनो-भावैर् वा ॥२९.३०॥ — or with clusters of flowers of gentleness and with beautiful feelings of mind.
29.translation: or with clusters of flowers of gentleness and with beautiful feelings of mind.

31.word_for_word: पौराः पुर-स्त्रियः ॥३१.३२॥ — The citizens and the women of the city.
31.translation: The citizens and the women of the city.

32.word_for_word: रजको वस्त्र-निर्णजकः स एव वस्त्राणां रङ्गम् अपि कुर्वन् रङ्ग-कारः । — A tailor is a cloth-maker, and he is also a dyer who dyes clothes.
32.translation: A tailor is a cloth-maker, and he is also a dyer who dyes clothes.

35.word_for_word: हे उद्वृत्ताः ! — O rescued ones!; गिरौ वने चरथ ये नित्यं ते यूयं पूर्वं परिधत्त इति सम्भावनायां लोट् । — Lot in the possibility that you, who are always wandering in the mountains and forests, have already worn them.; अभीप्सथ प्रार्थयध्वम् ॥३५॥ — If you desire, pray.
35.translation: O rescued ones! Lot in the possibility that you, who are always wandering in the mountains and forests, have already worn them. If you desire, pray.

36.word_for_word: राज-कुलानि राजकीयाः लुम्पन्ति निःस्वं कुर्वन्ति ॥३६॥ — The royalty plunder the royal families and deprive them of their property.
36.translation: The royalty plunder the royal families and deprive them of their property.

40.word_for_word: वायकस् तन्तु-वाय-विशेषः । — Vikas is a species of fibrous air.; वेषम् अलङ्कारम् । — Dress and ornaments.; चैलेयैर् वस्त्र-मयैर् अकल्पैर् भूषणैः ॥४०॥ — They were adorned with clothes and ornaments of various kinds
40.translation: Vikas is a species of fibrous air. Dress and ornaments. They were adorned with clothes and ornaments of various kinds

41.word_for_word: पर्वण्य् उत्सवे ॥४१॥ — in the festivals of the festivals.
41.translation: in the festivals of the festivals.

42.word_for_word: इह लोके परमां श्रियं च बलं चैश्वर्यं चेन्द्रियं तत्-पाटवं च प्रादात् ॥४२॥ — He bestowed upon me in this world supreme prosperity strength opulence senses and the path of that.
42.translation: He bestowed upon me in this world supreme prosperity strength opulence senses and the path of that.

46.word_for_word: क्षेमायाभयाय । — for the sake of safety and fearlessness.; भवायोद्भवाय ॥४६॥ — Bhavayodbhavaaya ॥46॥
46.translation: for the sake of safety and fearlessness. Bhavayodbhavaaya ॥46॥

47.word_for_word: रजक-वधेन वायकानुग्रहेण च युवयोर् विषम-दृष्टितयानीष्वरता नाशङ्कनीयेत्य् आह---न हि वाम् इति । — By killing the tailor and by showing mercy to the crow, there is no doubt that you two will be able to see each other differently.; अत्र हेतुः, समयोर् इति । — The reason here is, Samayor.; अत्रापि हेतु-द्वयम्, सुहृदोर् इति जगदात्मनोर् इति च ॥४७॥ — Here, too, there are two causes, namely, of the friend and of the soul of the universe.
47.translation: By killing the tailor and by showing mercy to the crow, there is no doubt that you two will be able to see each other differently. The reason here is, Samayor. Here, too, there are two causes, namely, of the friend and of the soul of the universe.

49.word_for_word: इत्य् अभिप्रेत्य इत्य् एवं विज्ञापयन्न् अभिप्रेत्य तन् मतं ज्ञात्वा । — He meant it, and thus he announced it, and he meant it, and he knew that opinion.
49.translation: He meant it, and thus he announced it, and he meant it, and he knew that opinion.

52.word_for_word: अन्वय-वर्धिनीं वंशे वृद्धि-मतीम् इत्य् अर्थः । — This means that she increases her consequences and increases her lineage.; अप्रार्थितं श्री-प्रभृतिकं च दत्त्वा ततो निर्जगामेति ॥५२॥ — Having given him unsolicited gifts such as Śrī and others he departed from there
52.translation: This means that she increases her consequences and increases her lineage. Having given him unsolicited gifts such as Śrī and others he departed from there
